card.title: Streaming LLM Tokens With Server-Sent Events
card.sub: SseEmitter on a virtual thread · Medium

a1.cap: Users shouldn't stare at a spinner while a model writes a long answer. Expose GET /api/chat/stream?q=... that streams each generated token to the browser as a Server-Sent Event, then sends a final done event.

lines: Users shouldn't stare at a spinner while a model writes a long answer. Expose GET /api/chat/stream?q=... that streams each generated token to the browser as a Server-Sent Event, then sends a final done event.

a1.cap: SseEmitter holds the response open and lets you push events with send. Run the generation on a separate (virtual) thread: for each token from the model, send a token event; finish with a done event and complete().
a1.say: Sse Emitter holds the response open and lets you push events with send. Run the generation on a separate (virtual) thread: for each token from the model, send a token event; finish with a done event and complete.

a1.cap: If the client disconnects, send throws, so stop and call completeWithError to free resources.
a1.say: If the client disconnects, send throws, so stop and call complete With Error to free resources.

a1.cap: The model client calls onToken for every token it generates.
a1.say: The model client calls on Token for every token it generates.

a1.cap: The endpoint produces text/event-stream, the Server-Sent Events format browsers understand.
The emitter keeps the response open for up to two minutes.
Generation runs on a virtual thread, so the request thread returns immediately.
Each token goes out as a named token event the moment it arrives.
A final done event tells the client the answer is complete.
On errors or a disconnected client, completeWithError closes the stream cleanly.
a1.say: On errors or a disconnected client, complete With Error closes the stream cleanly.
